name: Jix Media Library Cleanup Tool
author: Majix

sections.description:
The Jix Media Library Cleanup Tool is designed for WordPress administrators who want to keep their site lean and fast by removing unused or broken media files. Over time, your media library can become cluttered with “orphaned” attachments-database records that have no physical file, or files that are attached to deleted posts.

This tool provides a safe, iterative batch processing system to scan, detect, and clean these issues.

Core Features

Batch Processing: Scans attachments in small batches to prevent server timeouts, suitable for large libraries.

Dry Run Mode: Simulates the cleanup process and reports exactly what would be deleted without touching a single file.

Audit Logging: Generates a downloadable text log of every action taken.

Safety First: Supports moving files to the WordPress Trash (Soft Delete) before permanent deletion (requires config).

Manual Exclusions: “Lock” specific files in the Media Library to prevent them from ever being deleted.

Dashboard Widget: View quick stats about your library size and unattached items.

Pro Features

Deep Scan Engine: Scans Posts, Meta, and Options (Elementor/Divi support).

Automated Scheduler: Daily, Weekly, or Monthly cleanups.

Advanced Filtering: Filter by Parent Post Types and File Formats.
sections.installation:
Upload the media-cleanup-tool folder to the /wp-content/plugins/ directory.

Activate the plugin through the ‘Plugins’ menu in WordPress.

Navigate to Tools > Media Cleanup to start using the tool.
sections.faq:
Is it safe to use?

Yes. We strongly recommend using the Dry Run mode first.

How do I enable “Move to Trash”?

By default, WordPress media deletion is permanent. To enable the Trash for media files, add this to your wp-config.php:
define( ‘MEDIA_TRASH’, true );

My server times out during the scan.

Reduce the “Batch Size” setting to 5 or 10.

Where is the audit log stored?

The log is stored securely in your wp-content/uploads/media-cleanup-logs/ directory.
